title: Price your work, protect your orders, and show your skill

say: Price your work, protect your orders, and show your skill.
This is the video for Module 4 of Advanced Tailoring and Pattern Making.

Many skilled tailors earn less than they should, because they price by guessing. A good price covers four things. First, materials. Even when the client brings the lace, you buy lining, zips, thread and interfacing.

panel.heading: A price covers four things
items: Materials you buy: lining, zips, thread
Labour: your hours, including pattern work
Profit, so the business can grow

say: Second, your labour. Pattern work and fittings are skilled work, and belong in the price.

panel.heading: A price covers four things
items: Materials you buy: lining, zips, thread
Labour: your hours, including pattern work
Profit, so the business can grow

say: Third, overheads: rent, electricity, generator fuel and data, shared across the garments you finish each month.

panel.heading: A price covers four things
items: Materials you buy: lining, zips, thread
Labour: your hours, including pattern work
Profit, so the business can grow

say: And fourth, profit. If any one is missing, you are paying for the client's outfit yourself.

panel.heading: A price covers four things
items: Materials you buy: lining, zips, thread
Labour: your hours, including pattern work
Profit, so the business can grow

say: Ifeoma in Lagos is pricing a fitted lace gown. All these figures are approximate.
Lining, zip, thread, interfacing and boning come to about 8,600 naira.
She wants 250,000 naira a month and sews about 125 hours a month. That is 2,000 naira an hour. The gown takes 10 hours, including pattern adjustment and two fittings. That is 20,000 naira.
Her monthly overheads are 130,000 naira, shared over about 40 garments. That is 3,250 naira per gown.
Her total cost is 31,850 naira. With 25 percent profit, she quotes about 40,000 naira.
She now knows that charging 25,000 would mean losing money on every gown.
A one-off gown takes about 10 hours of labour, including 3 hours of pattern work just for that client.

In an aso-ebi group of 20, one base pattern is graded and shared, and you cut and sew in batches. Labour drops to about 5.4 hours a gown. So you may offer a lower price, but only after calculating it.
Set a cut-off date for measurements and deposits, and refuse orders that would push you past the event.
Agree a deposit before you cut, for example half the price, with the balance before collection.

cards.d: For example half the price before cutting, and the balance before collection.
Confirm money in your bank, Opay or Moniepoint app. Never trust an SMS or screenshot.
Order form: style, fabric received, price, deposit, fitting and delivery dates.

say: Fake bank transfer alerts are a known scam. Before you release a garment, check your own bank or wallet app, not an SMS or a screenshot from the customer.

cards.d: For example half the price before cutting, and the balance before collection.

say: And use a written order form. Most disputes come from things never written down: you said Friday, I wanted the neckline lower. Write the style, fabric received, price, deposit, fitting dates, delivery date and your alteration policy.

say: For example, Zainab in Abuja gets an order on 1 March for a lace gown for a wedding on 29 March. She works backwards from the event.

panel.heading: Zainab plans back from the wedding

say: From 1 to 4 March, consultation, measurements, deposit and the shrinkage test.

panel.heading: Zainab plans back from the wedding

say: Pattern and toile from 5 to 11 March.

panel.heading: Zainab plans back from the wedding

say: First fitting on 12 March, then sewing in lace.

panel.heading: Zainab plans back from the wedding

say: Final fitting on 22 March.

panel.heading: Zainab plans back from the wedding

say: Delivery on 26 March, three days before the wedding, so there is time for a last fix. She sends a WhatsApp reminder before each fitting.

say: To remember. Price from real costs, with profit on top, not instead of your labour. Calculate before you discount. Take a deposit and confirm every payment yourself. And plan fittings back from the event.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Hourly rate = income needed / hours sewn
Deposit first; confirm payment in your app
Plan back from the event with a buffer
